c.tagline: High-altitude Andean capital of art, coffee culture and endless nightlife.

taxi.fareNote: Meters run in a unit system (not direct pesos); ask driver or use apps like Cabify/Uber to avoid overcharging, especially from the airport.

emergency.note: 123 is the unified national emergency line reaching police, fire, and medical dispatch in Bogotá.

avoid.reason: Avoid Ciudad Bolívar and the southern peripheries.
Caution in La Candelaria at night and the Santa Fe red-light area; drink-spiking (scopolamine) in nightlife.

hood_desc: Colonial historic core with cobblestone streets, museums (Gold Museum, Botero Museum) and the presidential palace; best for first-time visitors who want to sightsee on foot, though it quiets down and feels less safe at night.
Bogotá's main nightlife and dining hub with the Zona T pedestrian plaza, upscale malls and clubs; suited to travelers who want walkable restaurants, bars and shopping close to their hotel.
Leafy, upscale district with colonial-style plaza, art galleries, craft breweries and fine dining; popular with families and travelers seeking a safer, quieter, more polished base in the north.
Bogotá's largest district, mixing LGBTQ-friendly nightlife (Chapinero Alto/Zona Rosa fringe), universities, and trendy cafes; good value and central for younger travelers and digital nomads.
Bohemian, artsy pocket next to Chapinero known for graffiti, indie boutiques, vintage shops and craft coffee bars; suited to travelers wanting a hip, walkable, mid-priced neighborhood.
lodging: AC Hotel Bogotá Zona T by Marriott

water.note: Tap water in Bogotá's modern, developed areas is treated and safe to drink; older buildings may vary.

transit.hours: TransMilenio operates roughly 4:30am-11:30pm daily; limited night bus service continues after; no 24-hour rail option exists.
transit.note: System is extensive but can be very crowded at rush hour; pickpocketing is a known risk on buses, so keep valuables secure.
transit.pay: Visitors buy or tap a rechargeable Tullave smart card (sold at station kiosks) to enter TransMilenio and SITP buses; cash is not accepted at turnstiles. Cards can be topped up at stations and many convenience stores.

bus: Intercity buses from Terminal de Transporte de Bogotá
train: Turistren heritage tourist train to Zipaquirá (weekends only, not a commuter service)

airport.drive: 20-40 min depending on traffic and destination neighborhood
airport.name: El Dorado International Airport (BOG)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to city center (35-50 min)

tip.r: Restaurants often add a voluntary 10% 'propina' line on the bill you can decline; taxis and casual services are not typically tipped.
